newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's top mining official sacked.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's top mining official sacked.

text.p: Indonesia on Monday replaced the top mines department official responsible for handling the controversial Busang gold find, officials said.
Officials in the Mines and Energy Ministry said Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, the director-general for general mining, was replaced by Adjat Sudradjat, director-general of geology and mining resources.
The officials said President Suharto signed a decree approving the changes on Wednesday and they took effect on Monday.
The officials said Adjat's current post would be taken by another official and that the director-general for electricity and energy development Zuhal was also being replaced.
There was no official word on the reason for the shake-up.
Kuntoro told reporters said he did not wish to comment on the reasons for his dismissal.
Asked if the move was related to the controversy over the Busang gold fields, he said: "Ask the minister."

Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper said on Saturday that Kuntoro's replacement would raise many questions because of his key responsibility in the handling of the Busang gold deposit in East Kalimantan province found by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd.
Bisnis Indonesia newspaper said the reasons for the change were not clear.

The Media Indonesia daily said it could be related to internal rivalries between a group of technocrats who once taught at the Institute of Technology Bandung (ITB) and those loyal to Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana, a retired general.
Kuntoro said on Monday that he was considering returning to a teaching job at the ITB.

Bre-X said last month the Busang property in East Kalimantan province might hold less than the 71 million ounces of gold it had earlier declared. The original amount would make it the gold find of the century.

"There appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang property...have been overstated because of invalid samples and assaying of those samples," Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in a statement last month.
But he said in an interview published in Canada on Sunday that he was confident the original estimates would hold up.

Industry sources said last week independent drilling tests of the Busang gold property are likely to be flown to Australia for analysis by mid-April with the results available by the end of the month.
